questions.question: Which three components together constitute domestic demand according to the speaker?
questions.answer: Household consumption, firm investment, and government expenditure
questions.explanation: The speaker defines domestic demand as the sum of household consumption, firm investment, and government expenditure (Q0002).

evidence.quote:
Domestic demand is whatever the household's demand,
 consumption, plus firm's investment,
 plus government expenditure.

options: Household savings, corporate profits, and taxes
Consumer confidence, interest rates, and exchange rates
Household consumption, firm investment, and government expenditure

original_segments.text: And now they're not.
So domestic demand remains the same as before.
Domestic demand is whatever the household's demand,
consumption, plus firm's investment,
plus government expenditure.
That's the same we had in closed economy.
This hasn't changed.
The domestic demand is the same.
It's a function of the same behavioral functions
that we had there. And the only two that we had was the consumption function and investment function.
So that remains the same. Nothing has changed. What does change is that this is no longer what
determines the demand for domestically produced goods. And remember, that's very key in the
short run because this Keynesian model with very sticky prices demand determines output activity.
So if we're going to determine domestic production from demand,
we better be very careful about what is the demand for domestically produced goods.
This is demand for both domestically produced goods and foreignly produced goods.
Some of those demands will be satisfied by imports.

questions.answer: The consumption function and the investment function
questions.explanation: The speaker states that the only two behavioral functions are the consumption function and the investment function (Q0007).

questions.question: According to the speaker, what has remained unchanged about domestic demand?
questions.answer: Its overall level remains the same
questions.explanation: Multiple excerpts (Q0005, Q0008, Q0009) emphasize that domestic demand is the same as before.

evidence.quote: The domestic demand is the same.

options: Its overall level remains the same
Its composition has shifted to include net exports
Its relationship with foreign demand has reversed
Its sensitivity to interest rates has increased

questions.question: What change does the speaker highlight regarding what determines demand for domestically produced goods?
questions.answer: It is no longer determined by domestic demand
questions.explanation: The speaker notes that what determines demand for domestically produced goods has changed; it is no longer domestic demand (Q0010).

evidence.quote:
What does change is that this is no longer what
 determines the demand for domestically produced goods.

options: It is now based on consumer price expectations
It is now solely determined by export demand
It is no longer determined by domestic demand
It is now driven by foreign exchange rates
